summary: Sacks attributes Robinhood's dramatic stock price appreciation (from ~$2 to a ~$130B market cap) to the crypto-friendly policies of the Trump administration, implying the regulatory tailwind is the key driver of value.
quote: what's the reason why your Robinhood stock is through the roof? Because of the crypto policies of the Trump administration. That's why it's gone from, what is it, like $3 to $130 billion?

summary: Gerstner argues NVIDIA has captured nearly 100% of incremental AI data center revenue due to its superior performance-per-watt ecosystem, trades at a lower P/E than when it was at $200/share, has no 'dark GPUs,' and generates ~$450B in cash flow '25–'27 — making bubble concerns overblown and the stock still attractive.
quote: Nvidia trades at a lower price-to-earnings multiple than it did when it was $200 a share... There is not a dark GPU in the world today. There's not going to be a dark GPU in the world next week.

summary: Sacks is bullish on AI compute demand broadly and believes NVIDIA's training dominance is secure, though he flags inference competition as the key open question for the stock's long-term trajectory.

summary: Jason highlights gold breaking $4,000 for the first time, up over 50% for the year, outpacing Bitcoin and major indices, and asks whether it's a safety trade, anti-USD trade, or money supply issue — framing it as a notable bullish phenomenon and giving a shout-out to a friend who called it.
quote: Gold rally is off the charts. Shout out to our friend Vinnie Langham, who told us about this for the last year or two. Geez, it just broke $4,000 for the first time ever this week, up over 50% for the year. Gold's outpacing Bitcoin, which is up 30% itself.

summary: Jason notes silver is surging even more than gold, attributing part of the move to industrial utilization demand.
quote: Silver is surging even more than gold. There might be some utilization reasons for that. Silver gets used in a lot of different components, whereas gold very rarely does.

summary: Chamath explains gold's rise as driven by net new buyers — chiefly Tether Gold stablecoin issuance, central bank rebalancing, and macro funds losing confidence in central bank policy and moving away from bonds and currencies into gold.
quote: Why is gold up? Gold is up because there are many more net new buyers. Who is the most important net new buyer? It's Tether... central banks are rebalancing... macro funds have essentially decided that central banks aren't to be trusted... so they're long gold.
topics: loss of confidence in central banks

summary: Brad (guest) affirms Chamath's view, pointing to new demand from crypto-native gold exposure (Tether Gold), geopolitical concern about government balance sheets, and gold's dual role as speculative asset and store of value — celebrating those up 50% this year.
quote: You have new demand for it. You do have people concerned about the state of the world, but it's always been a speculative asset plus a store of value... hats off to the people who are up 50% this year on gold.

summary: Sacks adds that China's central bank has been buying gold for 11 consecutive months and diversifying away from USD and US Treasuries, and that BRICS nations are exploring gold-backed settlement certificates — structural long-term tailwinds for gold demand.
quote: China's central bank has been increasing its gold reserves for 11 consecutive months... they've been gradually substituting away from US dollars and US treasuries towards gold... the BRICS talk about... some sort of gold-backed certificates where they can settle up huge international trade flows.
